title: Theoretical neuroscience
stage: Graduate study and research in neuroscience
audience: a graduate preparing for research in neuroscience or cognitive science, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD or a research role
purpose: Study the mathematical theory of neural computation at graduate level: dynamical systems for single neurons and networks, bifurcations and excitability, mean-field and population models, attractor dynamics and continuous attractors, balanced networks and irregular activity, information theory and neural coding, efficient and sparse coding, Bayesian brain hypotheses and neural sampling, synaptic learning rules and their stability, and low-dimensional dynamics in high-dimensional recordings, with the open questions of the field.
primary_reading: Neuronal Dynamics by Gerstner, Kistler, Naud and Paninski (free online)

weeks.1: Dynamical systems for neurons: fixed points, stability and bifurcations
weeks.9: The Bayesian brain and probabilistic population codes
weeks.10: Learning rules: Hebbian, BCM and their stability

blocks.deliverable: Classify the bifurcation of a two-variable neuron model.
Derive the balanced state of a two-population network.
Analyze the stability of a ring attractor.
Week 7 midterm; derive the efficient code for a supplied input distribution.
Analyze the stability of a Hebbian rule with normalization.
Write a referee-style critique of a theory paper.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Theory paper: choose one theoretical result (for example the balanced state, a ring attractor or an efficient-coding prediction), derive it carefully, verify it with a small simulation of your own, extend it in one direction, and write a workshop-style paper with the derivation, the numerical check and a discussion of how experiments could test it.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
